questions: Do slalom line_loss_events fall from 1.3 toward 1.0 or below, and does max_error drop below 0.06? Report completion_time for any slalom finish.
Does s-bend steering_oscillation stay under 0.35 with the tighter track (iteration 7: 0.311)?
Does the oval still finish 20/20 at about 1.8 s with wheel_track 0.09 m?
On the slalom, is the failure now overshoot at direction changes, or line loss at entry? Report the heading at first line loss if line loss persists.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 or the oval loses any trials, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep the iteration 7 design. If slalom line loss rises further, report the heading at first line loss so the next step can target controller entry speed rather than more turn authority.

intent: Keep the iteration 7 design (±0.036 m span at 0.012 m pitch, 12 mm footprints, lead y=0.06 m, lighter body at 0.6 kg and 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body_width 0.12 m). Change only wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.09 m to add turn authority at the slalom's direction changes. The Integrator should keep the weights and the kp/kd from iteration 7 unchanged where possible, so the race isolates the track change. Expected: slalom progress rises above 0.53, line_loss_events move to about 1.0 or below, max_error drops toward 0.06, and the oval holds 20/20 with the s-bend at 17/20 or better and steering_oscillation under 0.35.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that lower yaw inertia raised slalom progress (0.30 to 0.53) and s-bend jitter fell slightly, but line-loss events rose from 1.0 to 1.3. Yaw inertia has now been tested at 0.7 kg and 0.6 kg, so the next lever is the drivetrain's turn authority, tested here through wheel_track. Iteration 4 vs 1 also suggested that narrowing the track gives a small slalom gain without hurting the oval.
rationale: Iteration 7 (mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.12 m, lead 0.06 m, span ±0.036 m at 0.012 m pitch, 12 mm footprints, wheel_track 0.10 m) is the best so far at 707.2. The s-bend finished 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.311, under the 0.35 limit, and the oval held 20/20 at 1.79 s. The slalom is still 0/20, but it moved: mean progress rose from 0.30 to 0.53, and the best trial reached a score of 383. Line-loss events rose to 1.3 and max_error is 0.0653, past the 0.06 limit. Lower yaw inertia therefore helps the robot get further through the slalom, but it does not yet keep the line. Iteration 4 vs iteration 1 (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10) also gave a small slalom gain, which suggests turn authority is still the lever that moves the slalom. The Integrator's rule for a rising line loss says to return mass and body_length to 0.7 kg and 0.16 m only if s-bend oscillation exceeds 0.35. It does not (0.311), so I keep the lighter body. I change one variable: wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m, about 11 percent more turn authority for the same PWM difference. The oval has about 1.2 s of time margin, so the drivetrain can absorb this. Expected result: slalom progress keeps rising, with line-loss events near or below 1.0 and possibly the first slalom finishes. The main risk is s-bend jitter from higher effective turn gain, so steering_oscillation must be reported on all tracks.
